summary: Overall risk is low: no major weaknesses were found, and the traffic looks like Email.

executive_report.headline: No major weaknesses were found in the VPN setup (risk score 5/100).
executive_report.business_impact: No major weaknesses were found, so the VPN setup adds little business risk. Even though the traffic is encrypted, an observer can still tell that it carries Email traffic from packet sizes and timing.
top_actions: Keep the current settings and re-check them after any configuration change.

technical_report.protocol_identification: Session S1: IKEv2 IKE_SA_INIT Mode, ESP Tunnel Mode over IPv4
technical_report.cipher_suite_analysis: Session S1: AES-256-GCM + AEAD, hash SHA256, DH group 14
technical_report.sa_analysis: Session S1: lifetime unknown, replay protection on, PFS on, NAT-T off
technical_report.metadata_exposure: No session sends its peer identity in clear | Traffic type can still be inferred from packet sizes and timing even though ESP is encrypted
technical_report.compliance_notes: Session S1: meets the checked NIST guidance
technical_report.uncertainty_notes: Session S1: 11 of 16 values observed directly; inferred, not observed: ipsec_mode (packet-size heuristic: the smallest ESP payload leaves room for an inner IP header); replay_protection (ESP sequence numbers increased monotonically across 60 packets; the receiver's replay window itself is not visible on the wire); nat_traversal (IKE was seen only on UDP/500 in this capture); identity_exposed (IKEv2 always encrypts identity payloads, and none was seen in the clear); not determined: lifetime_seconds

traffic_analysis.metadata_inference: Medium to large packets (about 1224 bytes) about 3 ms apart, mostly upstream (99%), typical of sending email.

protocol.basis: version field of the IKE header

exchange_mode.basis: exchange type in the IKE header

ipsec_mode.basis: packet-size heuristic: the smallest ESP payload leaves room for an inner IP header

encryption.basis: encryption transform of the IKEv2 proposal

authentication.basis: the child SA proposal uses an AEAD cipher, which carries its own integrity check

hash.basis: PRF transform (AEAD suites negotiate no separate integrity algorithm)

dh_group.basis: DH transform of the IKEv2 proposal

key_exchange.basis: derived from the DH group number

auth_method.basis: method field of an AUTH payload seen in the clear (real IKEv2 encrypts it)

lifetime_seconds.basis: IKEv2 does not negotiate lifetimes on the wire

replay_protection.basis: ESP sequence numbers increased monotonically across 60 packets; the receiver's replay window itself is not visible on the wire

nat_traversal.basis: IKE was seen only on UDP/500 in this capture

identity_exposed.basis: IKEv2 always encrypts identity payloads, and none was seen in the clear

traffic_features.basis: measured from 60 ESP/AH packets (sizes and timing only)
